1. Endpoints of the first arc: P₁ = (95, 40) and P₂ = (41, 40). Distance |P₁P₂| = 95 − 41 = 54.
2. Arc radius r = 27, so 2r = 54 = |P₁P₂|. The chord is a diameter, so the arc is exactly a semicircle. The center is the midpoint (68, 40), and the large-arc flag is irrelevant in this case.
3. The second arc runs from (41, 40) back to (95, 40) with the same radius 27. Its endpoints are also diametrically opposite about (68, 40), so it is also a semicircle.
4. The sweep flags are both 0 (negative-angle direction). The first semicircle goes from angle 0° through −90° to 180° (the upper half in SVG's y-down screen coordinates). The second goes from 180° through 90° back to 0° (the lower half). Together they cover the full angle range once.
5. Two semicircles of radius 27 sharing the same center and joined at their endpoints form a full circle of radius 27 centered at (68, 40).

No other option fits: the path has no straight segments, corners, or vertices, and its two arcs have equal radii, so it is not an ellipse.

Final answer: (A) circle
